name: Single-Arm Rear-Delt Cable Fly
aliases: Single Arm Rear Delt Cable Fly
grip: Neutral grip on one D-handle with the wrist aligned with the forearm.
description: Open one arm away from a cross-body cable reach while keeping the torso and elbow bend nearly unchanged.
setup: Set one pulley around shoulder height and attach a D-handle.
Stand side-on to the stack and take the handle with the hand farther from the pulley.
Reach that arm across the upper chest, establish a small elbow bend and take up cable tension.
instructions: Sweep the working arm outward at approximately shoulder height.
Keep the elbow bend similar so the motion comes mainly from the shoulder.
Stop around the torso plane without twisting the body or pulling the elbow far behind.
Return slowly across the body, then repeat for the other side with the same setup.
cues: Open the arm in an arc.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbow into a row.
Turning the torso or shrugging to move the handle.

logging.example: One stack selected at 5 kg for each arm: record 5 kg per side and repetitions for each side.
logging.note: Use the same pulley height and machine for both sides. Do not sum the two sides' loads; stack markings and pulley ratios differ across machines.

variantNote: One hand-held cable, standing with a shoulder-height pulley. Cuff attachment, low-pulley bent-over and two-arm versions need separate instructions.
reviewNotes: Pulley height and D-handle are assumptions for the generic single-arm name.
Source describes bilateral standing cable reverse fly; unilateral execution is an editorial adaptation requiring technique review.

sources.title: Muscle & Strength - Standing Cable Reverse Fly
sources.scope: General standing reverse-fly shoulder action with a similar elbow bend. Source is bilateral; this draft adapts it to one arm and an explicitly stated pulley height.

illustration.alt: Two front-view line drawings of a single-arm cable rear-delt fly; the same right hand holds the handle in both positions.
